entities.summary:
The triboelectric effect is a phenomenon in which certain materials become electrically charged when they come into contact with other materials. 


It occurred during the Classical era of empires and foundational civilizations, a time when the ancient Greeks and Romans were developing their philosophical and scientific ideas. The triboelectric effect was first observed by the ancient Greek philosopher Thales of Miletus, who noted that rubbing amber against certain materials could create a static electric charge.


The triboelectric effect is a moderately significant entity in the historical record, and its understanding has had a lasting impact on our comprehension of the natural world. The discovery of the triboelectric effect led to a greater understanding of the fundamental principles of electricity, and it paved the way for later scientists such as Benjamin Franklin to explore the properties of electricity in more depth.


In more recent times, the triboelectric effect has been studied in the context of modern technologies such as electrostatic painting and the development of new materials with unique electrical properties.


For example, the triboelectric effect is responsible for the buildup of static electricity in clothing made from synthetic fibers, causing it to cling to human bodies.
